Phenomenon

/fuh-NOM-uh-non/ — four bouncing beats: 'fuh-NOM-uh-non' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Phenomenon is something observed to happen or exist, especially when it is hard to explain.

Scientists traveled from around the world to study the strange glowing phenomenon over the desert.

Worked Example

Every November, thousands of starlings gather over the marsh at dusk and swirl into vast, shifting shapes — ribbons, spheres, waves — with no leader directing them. Researchers film it every year and still debate how each bird knows exactly where to turn.

The birds' display is a phenomenon — something clearly observed yet hard to fully explain. An ordinary 'event' is easily understood; a phenomenon draws study precisely because it resists easy explanation.

How Phenomenon Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

marvel

marvel: something that causes wonder

occurrence

occurrence: something that happens

wonder

wonder: something astonishing to behold

Antonyms

commonplace

commonplace: an ordinary, unremarkable thing

routine

routine: a usual, fully expected happening

How Strong Is It? — event → phenomenon → miracle

event vs. phenomenon

event vs. phenomenon: Event is weaker than phenomenon — an event is any happening at all, while a phenomenon is striking enough to demand observation and explanation.

miracle vs. phenomenon

miracle vs. phenomenon: Miracle is stronger than phenomenon — a phenomenon is hard to explain, but a miracle seems to defy explanation entirely.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of phenomenon.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — phain-/phen-

root — phain-/phen-: to show, to appear (Greek)

suffix — -omenon

suffix — -omenon: that which is (participle ending) (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek phainomenon meant 'that which appears.' A phenomenon is something that visibly shows itself to observers — even when its cause stays hidden.

Use the root in a new word: phantom

Use the root in a new word: phantom: The old sailors swore a phantom ship appeared in the fog each winter.
